To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“In Zambian prisons, the interaction of environmental conditions, social and institutional factors, and human behaviours contribute to a complex and dynamic health and health services system that is characterized by inequity, poor access, and high disease burden.”
in the Zambians prisons, there is a high burden of communicable diseases due to overcrowding, poor sanitation and lack of access to quality health services.

in the context of resource scarcity, inequities in wealth and authority within the prison environment lead to a vicious cycle in which health and healthcare access are compromised, and inmate and officer-led coercion are common.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the prison environment, the prison system and the health system interact to affect health and healthcare access for inmates and officers.
the way in which the prison system as an entity interacts with its internal and external environment.
the ways that health systems can be better designed and implemented in prisons in SSA, in order to reduce disease burden and improve health and healthcare access for prisoners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Zambian prisons are not conducive to health and healthcare access, but rather that the health of inmates and prison officers is shaped by the complex interaction of facility-level social and environmental factors, and facility-level social and administrative factors.
there is a need for a comprehensive and detailed conclusion.
the prison system in Zambia is in dire need of improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a complex adaptive systems framework can help to unpack the interactions that contribute to poor health and healthcare access within the prison system.
the prison system is a complex system and that interventions should not focus on one component of the prison system, but rather on the system as a whole.
prison health systems are complex adaptive systems that are affected by a variety of internal and external factors that can be understood through a complex systems framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a health systems approach is necessary to understand the complexity of prison health and to identify effective and efficient solutions.

the prison setting presents a unique and challenging environment that requires a more comprehensive understanding of how health systems function in the context of complex social and environmental interactions.
health and healthcare in Zambian prison is not only a product of resource shortages, but of the interactions of resource shortages with the human actors within prisons.
